folded_items.summary: B1 (blocking): wing-commander-9b-fold-cycle-guard.yml grants only actions: read but fold-cycle-guard.yml's guard job needs actions: write for its gh workflow run call, so GitHub rejects the reusable-workflow call and the lost-cycle guard never starts.

B2 (blocking): a stop-only run's legs incorrectly include the stop leg, so fold-turn-act/fold-turn-dispatch enqueue for it and a stop queues behind the run it's meant to stop, regressing FR-005/SC-009/T072.
B3 (blocking): a redispatched implement run is never correlated in fold-cycle-guard.yml, so waiters stale-reclaim the live run's ticket and a second loss is never reported (breaks FR-016a).

B4: T047's inline release in fold-dispatch/action.yml is a no-op because it tries to release the implement token while the dispatch ticket still holds the queue head, and the error is silently swallowed.
B5: a run-url that the 30-second poll misses releases the implement ticket even when gh workflow run succeeded, silently dropping the cycle after a 30-minute timeout.
B7: ledger error messages (fold-queue-ledger.sh:695,728) are written to stdout, which every caller discards or captures, making ledger errors invisible.
B8: the T049 extension for implement-liveness only checks status in_progress/queued, missing 'waiting' (environment approval), long-held confirm-timeout act heads, and redispatched runs.

B9: the no-concurrency-group rule for admit/claim-dispatch/await jobs (item 1's fix) has no gate behind it, so a regression that reintroduces the claim inside dispatch-once's concurrency group would pass every gate.
B10: fold-cycle-guard.yml's re-dispatch still sends -f fold_queue_token= without the 422 retry T047 added elsewhere, and adoption.md's doc contradicts the actual behavior at :1461-1467.
Nits: stale 'Gate 126' references left after the T051 renumbering, a stale docstring path, stale comment text naming an old caller, and an unbounded requeue loop that could starve a dispatch.

Item 1 (B6, blocking): fold-turn jobs have no always() release of their own ticket on failure, and admit leaves a timed-out ticket enqueued, so a failed fold-turn-dispatch/act wedges the ticket until stale-after-minutes.

Item 2 (B3, blocking): fold-cycle-guard.yml's redispatch recording still uses the default success() gate and records new-run-id after the fallible gh issue comment call, so a failed comment or a missed poll leaves a live redispatched run uncorrelated, which can later break FR-016a via an empty round at ledger.sh:269.
Item 3 (B9, blocking): Gate 128 scenario 15 doesn't actually detect the regression it targets — injecting a claim-dispatch step into dispatch-once still passes all fold gates.

Item 4 (should ride same cycle): the uncorrelated grace reclaim in fold-queue-await.sh reclaims a live implement run's ticket after ~15 minutes if a poll missed it, contradicting the comment that says reclaim only happens if the run doesn't exist.

Item 5 (should ride same cycle): an orphaned act ticket for a run's own run_id blocks that same run's fold-turn-dispatch for up to 6 hours because the liveness extension renews against the waiter's own in_progress status.
Item 6 (should ride same cycle): fold-cycle-guard.yml's redispatch poll window opens minutes before the actual gh workflow run call, risking picking up another spec's run on a shared wrapper.

Nits: the remaining ::error:: lines in ledger.sh (peek-failure paths) still go to stdout where callers swallow them, and the 422-path ticket-ownership choice from T056 isn't documented in contracts/fold-cycle-guard.md.

Gate 87's hard-coded FIXTURES list and Gate 135 check 4 never actually compare the four new fixtures against their `expected` values, so reverting the same-run fix in both find_stop_request and find_stop_command_comment stays green.

Gate 135's self-test does not cover the CHECKS registry itself — deleting a check's registration from CHECKS leaves --self-test and the gate at 0 failures, and nothing asserts callers wire marker-branch/marker-base-sha.

The stop-cause wording (the `case "$STOP_CAUSE"` phrase block and the stop-cause→run-label expression) is pasted into six places in board-loop.yml instead of having one home, violating CLAUDE.md's "Shared logic has exactly one home" rule.
Review and readiness still pass needs.select.outputs.branch/base-sha to the stop-check composite instead of steps.pr.outputs.branch, so a fix→review chain in the same run records branch: null.
Triage's and review's outcome comments still say "route's own if: is #901's to fix," but #901 has merged and route's if: already handles stood-down.
A re-run of failed jobs keeps the same run id, so after a release that run's own record no longer moves the baseline — worth a docstring note.

Round-4 review item 1: the other-branch containment check from MF-48 wrongly fails a correct subfolder implement retry. The retry prompt's bare `git fetch origin` brings in branches that other lifecycles pushed at the same time, and the retry reuses the snapshot taken before the cycle agent. This breaks Story 2 / AS-5 and the contract's promise that branches other runs moved are left alone.
